document: Group B decision proposals — snapshot and causality

decisions.proposal: Freeze an immutable match-level definition manifest with catalog, effect-registry, balance-rules and ruleset release IDs plus a canonical content digest. Each CardInstance keeps a resolved mechanical definition snapshot and its definition digest. schema_version remains structural only.
evidence: data/card_game/effect-registry-candidate.v1.json has schema_version but no immutable release metadata
sistemas/gwent.py::novo_estado does not write a manifest
decisions.approved_rule: Each match freezes an immutable definition manifest with catalog, effect registry, balance rules and ruleset release IDs plus a verifiable content digest. Each CardInstance stores a resolved mechanical definition snapshot and per-definition digest. schema_version remains structural only.

decisions.proposal: Use one UUIDv4 operation_id per logical action and distinct UUIDv4 event_id values for each domain event. Store causal links, sequence, event source and targets. Persist operation result, state revision and generated events atomically; identical idempotency fingerprint replays the saved result, conflicting reuse rejects.
evidence: cartas_gwent_matches stores state_json and has no revision/idempotency columns
decisions.approved_rule: Use a UUIDv4 operation_id for each logical action and separate UUIDv4 event_id values for domain events. Events are ordered, append-only and causally linked. Same operation_id plus same fingerprint replays the stored result; conflicting fingerprint reuse rejects. Updated state, revision, operation result and generated events commit atomically.

options.A: Remove rarity-based effect amplification entirely, following card-game-balance-spec-v0.1.md: rarity is classification, not an effect multiplier.
options.B: Retain rarity amplification only for direct outputs of the resolving effect; reactive outputs never inherit root rarity unless their own contract explicitly opts in.

decisions.reason: Option A is more consistent with the existing balance specification and eliminates hidden cross-effect amplification. Option B preserves more legacy mechanics but requires causal attribution on every output.
evidence: Chama Negra + Vingança synthetic runtime reproduction
decisions.approved_rule: Rarity is classification only. It does not modify effect magnitude, thresholds, target count/selection, duration or other execution parameters. RARITY_EFFECT_BUDGET must not exist as an execution dependency in the new system.

decisions.proposal: Every reactive effect has its own source_effect_id and causal parent; it does not inherit rarity or parameters from the external effect that triggered it. Under BUF-001 option A this is an invariant; under option B it is a mandatory rarity boundary.
evidence: rarity pass currently scans global bonus deltas without source attribution
decisions.approved_rule: Reactive effects have their own source_effect_id and causal parent. They never inherit rarity or execution parameters from the external effect that triggered them.

decisions.proposal: Only active, verified catalog bindings become capabilities in the new effect registry. Orphan handlers and inactive aliases remain historical/compatibility records until explicitly rebound.
evidence: card-game-effect-catalog-decision-v0.1.md marks extraction as not connected to runtime
decisions.approved_rule: Only active, verified catalog bindings become capabilities in the new effect registry. Orphan handlers and inactive aliases remain historical/compatibility records until explicitly rebound.

decisions.proposal: A successful removal/sacrifice produces a removal event; if the removed unit has Vingança and the approved cause policy allows it, create a separate reactive Vingança event. A shield-blocked attempt is not a removal and does not trigger Vingança. Exact cause set remains a Group F decision.
evidence: Vingança branch runs after successful movement to discard
legacy sacrifice call uses the same removal helper
decisions.approved_rule: Successful normal_removal, execution or sacrifice emits a removal event; Vingança emits a separate reactive event only after successful removal. Shield-blocked attempts do not trigger it. The allowed cause set is fixed by approved FCAUSE-001/FCAUSE-004.

decisions.proposal: Represent Rykard's Vingança +1 and leader +2 as separate causal outputs with source IDs and ordered events. Legacy +3 is observed behavior, not a final approved design value.
evidence: Rykard leader handler removes victim then applies +2
legacy runtime fixture confirms +3 when victim has Vingança
decisions.scope_note: Causal separation is approved by Groups B and F; +1/+2/+3 legacy numbers remain balance parameters and are not frozen.

scope_note: Grupo B aprovado. RSRX-03 cause set is now closed by Group F; E-001..E-010 is approved separately. No runtime integration or production migration is implied.
